9/30/26 UPDATE: I cannot say enough wonderful things about Carnegie Hill Veterinary, and especially Dr. Facison.

Sadly, on September 25th, I had to say goodbye to my beloved cat Princess after discovering that she had cancer throughout her body. It was absolutely devastating, made even harder by the fact that my father had passed away just a few weeks earlier. When I shared what I had been going through, the compassion and kindness I received from everyone at Carnegie Hill Veterinary was extraordinary.

They could not have handled such a heartbreaking situation with more care, patience, and gentleness. So many members of the staff hugged me, offered their condolences, and treated both Princess and me with such genuine tenderness during one of the hardest moments of my life. I will never forget that.

Dr. Facison in particular is an exceptionally kind and caring person. I brought my other cat in today for a checkup, and the moment she saw me, she greeted me with a hug and so much warmth. That simple gesture meant more to me than she probably realizes.

There is something truly special about this practice. Everyone I have encountered has been kind, compassionate, and clearly devoted to the animals and people they care for. Losing Princess was heartbreaking, but I am incredibly thankful that I found Carnegie Hill Veterinary and that they were the ones who helped us through her final days.

I know my other cat is in wonderful hands here, and I fully expect that we will be coming to Carnegie Hill Veterinary for many, many years to come. I’m so grateful to Dr. Facison and the entire team. ❤️

9/16/26:
I took my 10-year-old cat to Carnegie Hill Veterinary for the first time today, and I am SO happy that I did. From the moment we walked in, everyone was incredibly kind and welcoming. You can immediately tell that the people here genuinely care about the animals they treat.

Dr. Facison was absolutely amazing. I honestly can’t say enough positive things about our experience. They were patient, listened to all of my concerns, explained everything clearly as they went along, and made me feel like my cat was truly being cared for rather than just being another appointment. Everything was communicated openly and transparently, including costs, which were presented in advance with no surprises. I also found the pricing very reasonable, especially for the Upper East Side of Manhattan.

Most importantly, they absolutely loved on my cat baby! ❤️ They handled her with so much gentleness, patience, and genuine affection, which meant everything to me. As anyone with a beloved pet knows, seeing someone treat your animal with the same kind of care and love you would is priceless.

I left feeling completely confident that we had found the right veterinary practice. I’m so grateful we came here, and after just one visit, I can confidently say Carnegie Hill Veterinary has earned some lifetime customers — both me and my cat baby! 🐱❤️
We appreciate Dr Facio’s expertise and support for our dog during his recent illness. The staff at Carnegie Hill is very friendly and caring. I highly recommend Carnegie Hill Veterinary Clinic.

This incident occurred about 6 months ago, but despite the length of time it still felt important to share with people considering this practice. TLDR, standard of care treatment was not given to my cat for an extremely common ailment and we were completely ignored, which led to undue stress and unnecessary wasting of time and money.

I had taken both of my cats to Carnegie Hill Vet for physicals last summer and had a great experience with Dr. Facison. Flash forward to fall of last year when one of my cat’s experienced an inflamed anal gland. I brought her in for a sick visit, described the symptoms to Dr. Stephanie Peck. She looked at my cat’s butt for no longer than 30 seconds, said “oh no, looks like it ruptured!”, took off her gloves, and then said we would give her an antibiotic and see her again in a week. My other cat has had 2 ruptured anal glands in the past, and both times the vets that cared for her flushed out the abscess, made sure the area was clean, and sent us home with a cone. None of this was done at Carnegie Hill Vet, which felt wrong - but I’m not a vet so what do I know?? This was a facility I trusted.

The next day I look at my cat’s butt and I am horrified. Her fur is matted, anal gland material is still leaking out, and when I attempt to clean the area I can tell she is in a great amount of pain and I do not feel comfortable handling this myself. This is on the weekend after hours, so I wait to contact Carnegie Hill until Monday morning. I call as soon as they open and am given instructions from a vet tech to clean the wound myself, which I am not comfortable doing but I oblige. I am told to send them pictures and that a doctor will call me, I’m also told to do so ASAP since they are closing early at 1pm (not advertised anywhere on their website). I immediately follow the instructions and send pictures and a detailed message as instructed. Over an hour passes, and 1pm is fast approaching, so I call and the person who picked up had no idea that I have even texted, but I’m assured I will get a call back. More hours pass, I send more texts, and I am completely ignored. 1:00 rolls by and I have gotten no response or call back.

So, I take matters into my own hands and take my cat to an event care vet, who is appalled. They immediately sedate her and flush out the wound, and explain to me that this is always the standard of care treatment for an anal gland rupture, as I had suspected. Upon reviewing the notes, they had to remove necrotic tissue from the wound, which should have NEVER been allowed to get to that point AFTER receiving medical treatment. My cat hates the vet and needs to be heavily medicated every time we go. Had this treatment been done at my initial visit as it should have been, we would have not wasted, time, money, and additional stress on myself and my cat!

Also, over 48 hours after I had contacted Carnegie Hill with my concerns and sent them pictures (as instructed) I still had not received ANY follow up. No text, no call, nothing after a patient reached out with complications and concerns. I only received a response when I texted saying that I would never be returning. I share this story because had I not been through this with my other cat at another provider, I may not have known that something was wrong and left my cat to suffer who who knows how long. The treatment we received was completely unacceptable and the quality amongst vets at this practice is inconsistent. I believe if Dr. Facison had seen my cat, this would not have happened, but I can’t trust a facility that would allow such negligence.

TL;DR: Rotating temp vets, no stethoscope used during a “full workup”, yet still recommended and unnecessary $650 echo — transferred care to Small Door Veterinary. Avoid if you value competent, consistent care, and reasonable pricing.

Carnegie Hill Veterinarians markets itself as a large practice, but the reality is you never know which vet will show up — in my case, it was a temp who had only been there twice and may not return for months.

During Theo’s visit, they didn’t even use a stethoscope to listen to his heart, yet insisted he needed a $650 echocardiogram before a dental cleaning. That’s like selling a car without checking the engine first.

After a second opinion, we transferred care to Small Door Veterinary, where the exam was thorough, the heart was actually listened to with a stethoscope, and a dedicated veterinarian provides consistent care. I was not upsold on anything, and their pricing was more reasonable and affordable.

If you care about transparency, continuity, or competent medical judgment, look elsewhere. This practice is disorganized, upsells procedures without justification, and leaves you guessing who will show up and what they’ll recommend next.
Everyone there is friendly and knowledgeable. Whenever I have an issue with my dog, they address it immediately. I am so thankful to have found them and highly recommend.
Friendly, helpful and knowledgeable!  Great experience.
Dr Hilchuck is an excellent Veterinarian she pays close attention to what you tell her about your pet.

Our one-year-old cat had a seizure at home, so we rushed him to this veterinary office for urgent help. When we arrived, the staff refused to see him and told us they “didn’t have time,” despite it being an emergency.

Instead, we were sent to an ER clinic more than 30 blocks away while our pet was actively in distress. This was an extremely frightening and disappointing experience, and we felt completely unsupported during a critical moment.

I understand that not every clinic can handle every emergency, but turning away a seizing animal without even evaluating him or offering immediate assistance is unacceptable.

I’m sharing this so other pet owners are aware and can plan accordingly in case of an emergency.
